title: Messiaen's mode in a Rhythm changes line
summary: Monk Rowe asks about a G flat over G7 in a Rhythm changes composition based on Messiaen's mode of limited transposition.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: But you’re funny, you just said something about, “It didn’t fit.” And I was looking at something that you did, and I don’t know if this is the first time ever but —
This is Rhythm changes and the compositional device that you are riffing on is Messian’s Mode of Limited Transposition #3. Do you recall this?
Do I have to call security? You pulled that off of that?
You’re a detective. This is like “This is Your Life.”

Well I’m asking about, this is minutiae but you’ve got this line going up, you’ve got B flat to G 7 and then there’s this line going up [scats] and it lands on a G flat under the G 7 chord. Okay so explain that to me. Why can you do that? Why can you have a G flat?
